title: “Udāyi, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye—desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. Sounds cognizable…
content: “Udāyi, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye—desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. Sounds cognizable by the ear … Odors cognizable by the nose … Tastes cognizable by the tongue … Tangibles cognizable by the body—desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. These, Udāyi, are the five strands of sensual pleasure. Whatever pleasure or joy arises in dependence on these five strands of sensual pleasure, that is called sensual pleasure, defiled pleasure, worldling’s pleasure, ignoble pleasure. I say that such pleasure should not be pursued, should not be developed, should not be cultivated, should be feared.”

title: Elder Mahākāla: One who does not know thus, Yet still creates attachments — The fool goes on, Experiencing suffering again and again. Therefore, one who…
content:
Elder Mahākāla:

One who does not know thus,
Yet still creates attachments —
The fool goes on,
Experiencing suffering again and again.
Therefore, one who knows
Does not create attachments.
I will not lie down
With my head broken.

title: “And how, monks, is there restraint? Here, monks, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is not attached to agreeable forms nor…
content: “And how, monks, is there restraint? Here, monks, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is not attached to agreeable forms nor repelled by disagreeable forms. He dwells with bodily mindfulness established, with an immeasurable mind. He knows as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Here, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are abandoned without remainder. When he tastes a flavor … When he cognizes a phenomenon with the mind, he is not attached to agreeable phenomena nor repelled by disagreeable phenomena. He dwells with bodily mindfulness established, with an immeasurable mind. He knows as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Here, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are abandoned without remainder. Thus, monks, is restraint.”

title: “Monks, if a monk lives without ardor in his practice, though he may wish: ‘May my mind be liberated from the defilements without clinging,’ yet…
content: “Monks, if a monk lives without ardor in his practice, though he may wish: ‘May my mind be liberated from the defilements without clinging,’ yet his mind is not liberated from the defilements without clinging. Why is that? It is because he has not developed. Not developed what? He has not developed the four foundations of mindfulness. He has not developed the four right efforts. He has not developed the four bases of spiritual power. He has not developed the five faculties. He has not developed the five powers. He has not developed the seven factors of enlightenment. He has not developed the Noble Eightfold Path.”

title: Elder Eraka: “O Eraka, painful are sensual pleasures! O Eraka, not happiness are sensual pleasures! One who desires sensual pleasures, desires suffering. One who does…
content:
Elder Eraka:
“O Eraka, painful are sensual pleasures!
O Eraka, not happiness are sensual pleasures!
One who desires sensual pleasures, desires suffering.
One who does not desire sensual pleasures, does not desire suffering.
O Eraka, know this as it is.”

title: “Monks, the eye is burning. Forms are burning. Eye-consciousness is burning. Eye-contact is burning. Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact — whether pleasant, painful, or…
content: “Monks, the eye is burning. Forms are burning. Eye-consciousness is burning. Eye-contact is burning. Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact — whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that feeling is burning. Burning with what? Burning with the fire of greed, the fire of hatred, the fire of delusion. I say it is burning with birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. The ear … The nose … The tongue is burning. Tastes are burning. Tongue-consciousness is burning. Tongue-contact is burning … The body … The mind is burning. Phenomena are burning. Mind-consciousness is burning. Mind-contact is burning. Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact … that feeling is burning. Burning with the fire of greed, the fire of hatred, the fire of delusion. I say it is burning with birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

title: “Venerable sir, what is the first jhāna?” “Here, venerable sir, a monk, secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the…
content: “Venerable sir, what is the first jhāna?” “Here, venerable sir, a monk, secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, accompanied by initial and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. This, venerable sir, is called the first jhāna.” “Venerable sir, how many factors does the first jhāna have?” “Venerable sir, the first jhāna has five factors. Here, a monk in the first jhāna has initial thought, sustained thought, rapture, pleasure, and unification of mind. Thus, venerable sir, the first jhāna has five factors.” “Venerable sir, how many factors does the first jhāna abandon and how many does it possess?” “Venerable sir, the first jhāna abandons five factors and possesses five factors. Here, a monk in the first jhāna has abandoned sensual desire, abandoned ill-will, abandoned sloth and torpor, abandoned restlessness and remorse, abandoned doubt; he possesses initial thought, sustained thought, rapture, pleasure, and unification of mind. Thus, venerable sir, the first jhāna abandons five factors and possesses five factors.”

title: “Short is this life — Within a hundred years one dies, And even if one lives longer, One dies of old age. People grieve for…
content:
“Short is this life —
Within a hundred years one dies,
And even if one lives longer,
One dies of old age.

People grieve for what they hold as ‘mine’ —
All possessions are impermanent.
Seeing this, one should live homeless.

What people think of as ‘mine’
Is destroyed by death.
Knowing this, the wise one
Would not incline toward ‘mine.’

As when a person wakes up,
He no longer sees what appeared in a dream,
So too, a beloved person who dies
Is no longer seen.

Those who are seen and heard
Are called by such and such a name —
Only the name remains
For one who has passed away.

People who are greedy for ‘mine’
Do not abandon sorrow, lamentation,
And stinginess.
Therefore, sages, leaving behind attachments,
Live seeing safety.”

title: “Monks, I will teach you about suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering. Listen.…
content: “Monks, I will teach you about suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering. Listen. And what, monks, is suffering? It should be said: the five aggregates of clinging. What five? The form aggregate of clinging … the consciousness aggregate of clinging. This, monks, is called suffering. And what, monks, is the origin of suffering? It is this craving that leads to renewed existence … craving for non-existence. This, monks, is called the origin of suffering. And what, monks, is the cessation of suffering? It is the remainderless fading away and cessation of that same craving, the abandoning and relinquishing of it, freedom from it, non-reliance. This, monks, is called the cessation of suffering. And what, monks, is the path leading to the cessation of suffering? It is the Noble Eightfold Path, namely: right view … right concentration. This, monks, is called the path leading to the cessation of suffering.”

title: “Monks, these five things, when developed and cultivated, lead to the destruction of the defilements. What five? Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating foulness in…
content: “Monks, these five things, when developed and cultivated, lead to the destruction of the defilements. What five? Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating foulness in the body, with the perception of disgust for food, with the perception of non-delight in the entire world, contemplating impermanence in all formations, and the perception of death is well established within him. These five things, monks, when developed and cultivated, lead to the destruction of the defilements.”
